soundness_flags.one_line: The quantitative minimum-singular-value lower bound is a compact inference-subclass strengthening, not the cited paper’s standard unique-solvability condition; retag it novel with an inference justification or cite a source establishing this exact margin convention.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2, equations (2)–(6); Section 4, Theorem 2 and equations (18)–(19).
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published model permits a coefficient to be zero whenever its graph edge exists, defines observational distribution-set equivalence, and gives a graphical children-bases criterion for irreducible latent cyclic LiNG models.

Proposition 5.1 says observational and interventional distributions recover row i of W, and Section 5.1 interprets this as revealing one matching edge. The paper contains no “Theorem 5” and does not state the core’s displayed projection/lift/matching-set equality.
The paper characterizes I-Markov equivalence for latent DAG causal Bayesian networks using hard-intervention do-constraints and augmented MAGs, and gives a sound learning algorithm.

The paper develops necessary and sufficient experiment-design conditions and a complete search algorithm for recovering linear cyclic models with latent variables from experimental means and covariances.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3.2, Definition 3.3 and Theorem 3.6; Section 3.4, Proposition 3.8; Appendix C reference at p. 2899.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines unique solvability, establishes its intervention consequences, and notes that the linear case converts solvability to matrix invertibility; it does not formulate a uniform lower singular-value margin.
The paper derives cross-order cumulant rank restrictions for linear non-Gaussian SEMs, including latent-confounded models, and combines rank-based goodness-of-fit tests.
